latest_user_report: User suspects the power inductor as the smoke source and clarifies that the event occurred when USB power was connected. Source and component damage are not yet physically verified.

current_configuration.note: Nominal switching-current limits apply to a functioning IC with a valid ISET resistance. They do not constrain an external short directly discharging the capacitor bank through L1.

review.usb_replug_inrush: USB-to-SYS-capacitor inrush does not pass through L1. Normal capacitor charging through L1 is controlled by MAX38890.
review.timing_correction: A permanent external LX-to-GND short can discharge an already charged capacitor through L1, but does not itself establish a USB-to-L1 inrush path. When the IC high-side switch turns on into such a short, the direct USB short path is through that switch and the LX bridge, bypassing L1. The previous LX-to-GND explanation alone does not explain this power-connection event.
review.abnormal_uncontrolled_charge_path: An external SYS-to-LX bridge or failed shorted high-side switch could connect USB/SYS to L1 and CAP without normal switching-current control; this is an unverified fault hypothesis, not an expected effect of normal voltage difference.
review.copper_loss_comparison: At 5 A RMS, I^2*R gives 0.01675 W copper loss; this excludes core and AC losses and is not a full temperature prediction.
priorities: Confirm the fitted L1 part number and actual smoke location.
Inspect U1 LX pins and exposed ground pad, L1 pad surroundings, and conductive debris for physical bridges.
Check R8/R10 actual values and ISET pin 12 for unintended grounding.
Consider damaged U1 internal switches and hot solder joints or flux near L1; do not infer an L1 winding failure from smoke proximity alone.
review.safety: Keep USB disconnected. Do not short the capacitor bank to discharge it. No energized diagnostic test was performed.
